t: Listen to a talk in an economics class.
Microfinance means providing very small loans to people who can't get credit from regular banks.
Usually these borrowers are small business owners in rural areas—someone who wants to buy a sewing machine or a few goats.
Instead of asking for property as a guarantee, many lenders ask borrowers to form groups of five.
If one person can't pay, the others in the group help out, so members encourage each other to repay on time.
Critics point out that interest rates can be high, because it's expensive for lenders to manage thousands of tiny loans.
Still, repayment rates are often surprisingly strong.
